description:
Change who can open a module, run its activities, see its fields and table columns, see its listings, print its templates (documents) and use its actions. Call get_module_access first: its `options` name the people-module fields a grant can use, its `targets` the names that can be protected.

- Only the items you name change; each named item's rules are replaced. Send "everyone" to remove an item's rules.
- Rule forms: "everyone"; "nobody" (only platform administrators); {allow: [...]} — only these; {deny: [...]} — everyone except these; {allow, deny} — only the allowed, minus the denied.
- Grantees: "guest", {member: username}, {profile: people module}, or {profileField, in: [values], profile?} — the position grant, e.g. {profileField: "Position", in: ["Manager"]}. Listing grants are not supported.
- Precedence: the more specific grantee wins — member › profile field › profile › guest › everyone; within one kind, allow beats deny. So a Position allow plus a Department deny does not keep out people who match both (the platform warns).
- Preview with dryRun: true and show the user `changes` and `warnings` (`self_not_matched` means the change locks the user themself out).
- A change that lets in anyone who is kept out today returns access_change_requires_confirmation and saves nothing: show the user `changes`, and resend with confirmed: true only after they approve.
- To protect a field you just added with update_module, call this straight away; if it fails, tell the user the field is open.

access.description: The items to change, by name: { module?, activities?, fields?, listings?, documents?, actions? }. See UnitRule in inistate://schema/configure.

actions.description: By action name: who can use the action (a custom button)

activities.description: By activity name: custom activities, the standard ones (Create, View, Edit, Delete, Change State, …) and Import

documents.description: By print template name: who can print it

columns.description: A table field's columns, by column name. A field entry with only columns leaves the field's own rule as it is

fields.description: By field name: who can see (and so edit) the field. A restricted field is removed from forms, listings and history

listings.description: By listing name: who sees the listing

allow.description: Only these get in (everyone else is kept out)

in.description: With profileField: the values that match, e.g. ["Manager", "Director"]

profile.description: A people module: everyone with an entry in it. With profileField: the people module the field is on (needed only when two have it)

profileField.description: The position grant: a people-module field, e.g. Position

deny.description: These are kept out. Alone: everyone except them

others.description: "allowed" with deny + allow: everyone except the denied, and the allowed even if denied

replaceLegacy.description: Required to rewrite an item that still has obsolete listing grants (see the item's legacy in get_module_access)

module.description: Who can open the module at all

confirmed.description: Set only after the user explicitly approved a change that lets more people in

dryRun.description: Report the changes and warnings without saving

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID for this call. The MCP keeps no workspace between calls, so pass it every time; omit only when INISTATE_WORKSPACE_ID is configured.

name: set_module_access
title: Set Module Access
